title: Accountancy: Unit-wise Group A Question Bank

toc.title: 2.8 System of Government Accounting in Nepal
2.15 Use of Information Technology in Office and Accounting

html:
Group A of the SEE Accountancy paper is eleven very short answer questions of one mark each, all compulsory, drawn from every unit of the syllabus. Almost nothing in them is a long calculation: they test a definition, a name, a code, a formula, a one-step figure or a one-line journal voucher. They can be answered in about fifteen minutes, and they are the cheapest eleven marks in the paper. This chapter drills all fifteen units in order. Each section opens with a short facts line — what the one-mark questions from that unit keep returning to — and then gives ten questions with a key.

How to use this chapter

Read the facts line, answer the ten questions in writing, then check the key. Mark every question you got wrong on a single sheet; that sheet, not the whole book, is what you revise in the last week. Every question is an original practice question written to the pattern; none is claimed to have appeared in any year's paper.

2.1 Office Management and Procedure

Facts. Office management is planning, organising, directing, coordinating and controlling office work. Its areas are personnel, layout, machines, records, forms, procedures and financial work. Office procedure: receipt, sorting, recording, action, noting, drafting, approval, dispatch, follow-up. Filing = store; indexing = find. Layout is open, closed or mixed.

  1. Define office management. [1]
  2. Write any two areas of office management. [1]
  3. Name any two office procedures related to decision making. [1]
  4. What is office layout? [1]
  5. What is a noting? [1]
  6. What is drafting? [1]
  7. Define filing. [1]
  8. What is indexing? [1]
  9. Write any two objectives of filing. [1]
  10. What is meant by the retention period of a record? [1]
Answers

1. Office management is the task of planning, organising, directing, coordinating and controlling the work of an office so that its objectives are achieved efficiently and economically.

2. Any two of: personnel; layout and environment; machines and equipment; records management; forms and stationery; communication; financial office work.

3. Any two of: receipt and sorting, recording, action, noting and drafting, approval and signature, dispatch, follow-up.

4. Office layout is the arrangement of furniture, machines, departments and staff within the available floor space so that work flows smoothly.

5. A noting is the written record of the facts of a case, the applicable rules, the views of the sections concerned and a proposed decision, written on the file for the deciding officer.

6. Drafting is the preparation, in the form in which it will be issued, of a letter or order to be sent out of the office.

7. Filing is the systematic arrangement and storage of documents so that any document can be traced and produced when needed.

8. An index is a guide that tells where a particular record is kept — it converts a name or subject into the file's address.

9. Any two of: to keep papers safe; to make documents easy to trace; to keep related papers together; to preserve evidence; to serve as the office memory; to save space and cost.

10. The retention period is the fixed length of time for which a class of record must be kept before it may be transferred or destroyed.

2.2 Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutions

Facts. Nepal Rastra Bank (the central bank) — 26 April 1956 A.D. (2013 B.S.). Nepal Bank Limited — 1994 B.S. (1937 A.D.), the first bank of Nepal. Agricultural Development Bank — 2024 B.S. Banking institutions create credit; non-banking institutions do not. Insurance works by pooling risk. A cheque is open, order or crossed.

  1. What is a financial institution? [1]
  2. When was Nepal Rastra Bank established? [1]
  3. Write any two functions of a central bank. [1]
  4. Name the first bank of Nepal with the year of its establishment. [1]
  5. What is credit creation? [1]
  6. What is insurance? [1]
  7. Write any two kinds of non-life insurance. [1]
  8. What is meant by crossing a cheque? [1]
  9. What is remittance? [1]
  10. Distinguish between the money market and the capital market in one line. [1]
Answers

1. A financial institution is an institution whose main business is to collect money from savers and lend or invest it for those who need it, and to provide financial services such as deposits, loans, payments, insurance and foreign exchange.

2. 26 April 1956 A.D. (13 Baisakh 2013 B.S.).

3. Any two of: issuing currency; banker to the government; banker's bank; lender of last resort; monetary policy; foreign exchange management; supervision of banks; clearing house.

4. Nepal Bank Limited, 1994 B.S. (1937 A.D.).

5. Credit creation is the power of a bank to expand the supply of money by lending: a loan is credited to the borrower's account and becomes a new deposit, which supports further lending.

6. Insurance is a contract in which the insurer, in return for a premium, agrees to pay a stated sum to the insured if a stated event happens.

7. Any two of: fire, marine, motor, health, accident, crop and livestock insurance.

8. Crossing means drawing two parallel lines across the face of a cheque, directing the bank to pay it only into a bank account and never in cash.

9. Remittance is money sent by a person working away from home, usually abroad, to a person at home.

10. The money market deals in short-term funds and securities of up to one year; the capital market deals in long-term securities of more than one year.

2.3 Introduction to Tax

Facts. VAT in Nepal from 1 Mangsir 2054 B.S., under the VAT Act 2052 and Rules 2053, at a single rate of 13 per cent. PAN is a nine-digit permanent number from the Inland Revenue Department. Direct tax cannot be shifted; indirect tax is. Adam Smith's canons: equality, certainty, convenience, economy.

  1. What is tax? [1]
  2. What is indirect tax? [1]
  3. Write any two examples of direct tax. [1]
  4. Write the full form of VAT. [1]
  5. When was VAT introduced in Nepal? [1]
  6. What is the present rate of VAT in Nepal? [1]
  7. Write the full form of PAN and state how many digits it has. [1]
  8. Write any two sources of revenue of the Government of Nepal. [1]
  9. What is a progressive tax? [1]
  10. Write any two objectives of taxation. [1]
Answers

1. Tax is a compulsory contribution imposed by the government on persons, goods, services and transactions to meet public expenditure, without a direct and proportionate return to the payer.

2. An indirect tax is a tax imposed on one person but borne by another — the burden is shifted to the final consumer.

3. Any two of: income tax, house and land tax, capital gains tax, vehicle tax.

4. Value Added Tax.

5. 1 Mangsir 2054 B.S.

6. 13 per cent (a single rate).

7. Permanent Account Number; nine digits.

8. Any two of: income tax, VAT, excise duty, customs duty, land and house tax, vehicle tax, registration fees, royalties, dividends from public enterprises, foreign grants.

9. A progressive tax is one whose rate rises as the income or wealth of the taxpayer rises, so the rich pay a larger share of their income than the poor.

10. Any two of: to raise revenue, to redistribute income, to control inflation, to protect domestic industry, to discourage harmful consumption, to encourage saving and investment.

2.4 Business Accounting

Facts. Assets = Liabilities + Capital. The accounting cycle: journal, ledger, trial balance, adjustments, final accounts, communicate. Standards are issued by ICAN through its Accounting Standards Board: NFRS, NFRS for SMEs, NAS. The chart of accounts has five groups: assets 1, liabilities 2, capital 3, income 4, expenses 5.

  1. Define accounting in one sentence. [1]
  2. Write the accounting equation. [1]
  3. Name any two types of accounting. [1]
  4. What is an accounting standard? [1]
  5. Name the body that issues accounting standards in Nepal. [1]
  6. Write the full form of NFRS. [1]
  7. What is a chart of accounts? [1]
  8. Write any two external users of accounting information. [1]
  9. On which side is an increase in a liability recorded? [1]
  10. Distinguish between book-keeping and accounting in one line. [1]
Answers

1. Accounting is the process of identifying, measuring, recording, classifying, summarising and communicating economic information to those who need it.

2. Assets = Liabilities + Capital.

3. Any two of: financial accounting, cost accounting, management accounting.

4. An accounting standard is a written rule issued by an authorised professional body prescribing how a transaction or event must be recognised, measured, presented and disclosed in the financial statements.

5. The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ICAN), through its Accounting Standards Board.

6. Nepal Financial Reporting Standards.

7. A chart of accounts is the complete, organised and numbered list of all the account heads used to record transactions, grouped into assets, liabilities, capital, income and expenses.

8. Any two of: banks and lenders, suppliers and creditors, the government and the tax authority, investors, auditors, the public.

9. On the credit side.

10. Book-keeping is only the recording of transactions in the journal and ledger; accounting goes further and includes summarising, analysing and interpreting the recorded data and preparing the final accounts.

2.5 Bank Reconciliation Statement

Facts. Cash book = the trader's record; passbook = the bank's record. A debit balance in the cash book is a credit balance in the passbook. Cheques issued but not presented are added to the cash book balance; cheques deposited but not collected are less. Bank charges and interest on overdraft are less; interest allowed and direct deposits are added.

  1. What is a bank reconciliation statement? [1]
  2. Write any two causes of the difference between the cash book and the passbook. [1]
  3. What does a debit balance in the cash book (bank column) mean? [1]
  4. If the cash book shows an overdraft, what kind of balance does the passbook show? [1]
  5. A cheque issued but not presented makes the passbook balance higher or lower than the cash book balance? [1]
  6. Write any two items recorded by the bank only. [1]
  7. What is the adjusted cash book? [1]
  8. A cheque deposited is dishonoured. Which book shows it first? [1]
  9. Why is a bank reconciliation statement prepared? Give any one reason. [1]
  10. Name the statement prepared to bring the cash book and the passbook into agreement. [1]
Answers

1. A statement prepared on a particular date to explain and reconcile the difference between the balance of the bank column of the cash book and the balance of the passbook.

2. Any two of: cheques issued but not presented; cheques deposited but not collected; bank charges; interest allowed or charged; direct deposit by a customer; standing instructions; dishonoured cheque; errors.

3. Money is lying in the bank — a favourable balance.

4. A debit balance (an overdraft in the cash book is a debit balance in the passbook).

5. Higher — the trader has already reduced his cash book, the bank has not.

6. Any two of: bank charges and commission, interest allowed or charged, dividend collected, direct deposit by a customer, standing instructions, dishonour of a cheque.

7. The cash book after all items appearing only in the passbook have been entered in it, so that the remaining difference is only a matter of time.

8. The passbook.

9. To check the accuracy of both records and find errors; to find the true bank balance; to detect dishonoured cheques and unrecorded charges; to prepare the balance sheet; to prevent fraud.

10. The bank reconciliation statement.

2.6 Accounting Errors

Facts. One-sided errors affect the trial balance and need a suspense account; two-sided errors do not. Errors of principle, complete omission, compensating errors and the wrong account of the same class never affect the trial balance. The suspense account is credited when the debit column of the trial balance is short, and debited when the credit column is short.

  1. What is an accounting error? [1]
  2. What is an error of principle? Give one example. [1]
  3. What is a compensating error? [1]
  4. Which errors are detected by the trial balance? [1]
  5. Which errors are not detected by the trial balance? [1]
  6. What is a suspense account? [1]
  7. If the debit column of the trial balance is short, on which side is the suspense account opened? [1]
  8. A purchase of machinery was debited to the purchases account. What kind of error is this? [1]
  9. Where is a debit balance of the suspense account shown in the balance sheet? [1]
  10. Pass the rectifying entry: rent paid Rs. 6,000 was debited to the wages account. [1]
Answers

1. An accounting error is a mistake in recording, posting, casting, carrying forward or summarising a transaction, or in applying an accounting principle.

2. A mistake in applying an accounting rule, such as treating a capital expenditure as a revenue expense. Example: wages paid for installing a machine debited to the wages account instead of being added to the machine's cost.

3. One of two or more errors, each of the same amount and on opposite sides, which cancel each other so that the trial balance still agrees.

4. One-sided errors: casting and balancing errors, posting to the wrong side, a wrong amount posted in one account only, partial omission.

5. Two-sided errors: errors of principle, complete omission, compensating errors, wrong account of the same class, a transaction entered twice in both accounts.

6. A suspense account is a temporary account opened to hold the difference in the trial balance until the errors causing it are found and corrected.

7. On the credit side.

8. An error of principle.

9. On the assets side.

10. Rent A/c Dr. 6,000; To Wages A/c 6,000.

2.7 Final Account

Facts. Gross\ profit = Sales - Cost\ of\ goods\ sold; Cost\ of\ goods\ sold = Opening\ stock + Purchases + Direct\ expenses - Closing\ stock. Net\ profit = Gross\ profit + Other\ income - Indirect\ expenses. Every adjustment has two effects. Net profit is added to capital; drawings are deducted.

  1. What are final accounts? [1]
  2. Write the formula for the cost of goods sold. [1]
  3. How is outstanding salary treated in the final accounts? [1]
  4. What is the treatment of prepaid rent? [1]
  5. Where does the closing stock appear? [1]
  6. Where is the net profit shown in the balance sheet? [1]
  7. How are drawings treated in the balance sheet? [1]
  8. What is a provision for doubtful debts? [1]
  9. Write any two direct expenses. [1]
  10. What are accounting notes? [1]
Answers

1. Final accounts are the statements prepared at the end of the accounting period, after adjustments, to show the profit or loss of the period and the financial position on the closing date — the trading account, the profit and loss account and the balance sheet.

2. Cost\ of\ goods\ sold = Opening\ stock + Purchases + Direct\ expenses - Closing\ stock.

3. Added to the salary on the debit side of the profit and loss account and shown as a current liability in the balance sheet.

4. Deducted from rent on the debit side of the profit and loss account and shown as a current asset in the balance sheet.

5. Credited in the trading account on the credit side and shown as a current asset in the balance sheet.

6. Added to the capital on the liabilities side.

7. Deducted from the capital on the liabilities side.

8. An amount set aside out of profit to cover debts expected not to be recovered; it is debited to the profit and loss account and deducted from debtors.

9. Any two of: carriage inward, freight, wages, factory rent, fuel and power, customs and clearing charges.

10. Accounting notes are the explanations attached to the financial statements stating the accounting policies used, describing each item and disclosing contingent liabilities and other matters that the figures alone do not show.

2.8 System of Government Accounting in Nepal

Facts. Cash basis; double entry; fund basis; uniform formats and chart of accounts; budget classification; two levels of accounting; banking arrangement; audit by the Office of the Auditor General. Regulated by the Financial Procedures and Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2076 and Rules, 2077. FCGO = Financial Comptroller General Office.

  1. What is government accounting? [1]
  2. Write any two bases of government accounting in Nepal. [1]
  3. Which basis of accounting does the Government of Nepal follow? [1]
  4. Which office manages government accounting in Nepal? [1]
  5. What is a consolidated fund? [1]
  6. Write any two government offices that use central level accounting. [1]
  7. What is operating level accounting? [1]
  8. What is a chart of accounts? [1]
  9. Write any two areas of government accounting. [1]
  10. Name the apex auditing body that audits government accounts in Nepal. [1]
Answers

1. Government accounting is the system by which a government records, classifies, summarises and reports its revenue, expenditure and financial position, in order to be accountable to the legislature and the public for public money.

2. Any two of: legal basis; cash basis; double-entry system; fund basis; uniformity of forms and chart of accounts; budget classification; two levels of accounting; banking arrangement; external audit.

3. The cash basis.

4. The Financial Comptroller General Office (महालेखा नियन्त्रक कार्यालय).

5. The government's main fund, into which all revenue must be deposited and from which nothing may be withdrawn except under an appropriation made by law.

6. Any two of: the Ministry of Finance, the Office of the Auditor General, a ministry or department at the centre, the Financial Comptroller General Office.

7. The accounting of the transactions of a district or local office, kept in the office itself in the bank cash book and reported monthly through the statement of expenditure.

8. The uniform, coded list of every revenue head, expenditure head, fund and asset a government office may use, prescribed by the FCGO.

9. Any two of: revenue accounting, expenditure accounting, store accounting, fund accounting, deposit and retention accounting, loan and grant accounting, asset and liability accounting.

10. The Office of the Auditor General.

2.9 Revenue Accounting

Facts. Revenue must be deposited into the consolidated fund the same day. Codes: 11000 the tax group (11111 income tax on individuals), 14000 the non-tax group (14224 examination fee, 14227 passport fee, 14251 company registration fee, 14151 rent of government property, 14311 judicial fine). Check: revenue collected = amount deposited + cash in hand.

  1. What is revenue accounting? [1]
  2. Why must revenue be deposited into the bank on the same day? [1]
  3. What is a revenue statement? [1]
  4. Write the code for examination fee. [1]
  5. Write any two examples of non-tax revenue with codes. [1]
  6. What is a revenue voucher (आम्दानी भौचर)? [1]
  7. To which office is the monthly revenue statement sent? [1]
  8. May a government office pay its electricity bill out of the revenue it has collected? [1]
  9. Write the formula for checking a revenue statement. [1]
  10. Write any two objectives of revenue accounting. [1]
Answers

1. Revenue accounting is the branch of government accounting that records the collection of government revenue, its deposit into the consolidated fund through the bank and its reporting.

2. Because revenue must reach the consolidated fund and be accounted for, and an office that held it as cash could spend it outside the budget.

3. The monthly return (राजस्वको फाँटबारी) showing head by head the revenue collected, the amount deposited and the cash still in hand.

4. 14224.

5. Any two of: 14227 passport fee; 14251 company registration fee; 14151 rent of government property; 14221 judicial fee; 14311 judicial fine.

6. The voucher by which revenue is recorded in the accounts, naming the head, the payer, the amount and the evidence.

7. The Treasury and Comptroller Office (कोष तथा लेखा नियन्त्रक कार्यालय).

8. No. The revenue must be deposited in full and the bill paid under an appropriation, through a payment order and the bank cash book.

9. Revenue collected = amount deposited into the consolidated fund + cash still in hand.

10. Any two of: to record every rupee with evidence; to ensure deposit into the consolidated fund; to compare collection with the estimate; to detect leakage; to supply the government's financial statement; to keep the account public.

2.10 Accounting of Government Expenditure

Facts. Available\ balance = Appropriation - Expenditure - Uncleared\ advances. Expenditure codes: 2 recurrent (21111 remuneration, 22111 uniform, 22311 office materials, 22612 fuel, 22711 miscellaneous), 3 capital (31111 machinery, 31121 furniture). Bank cash book = म.ले.प.फा.नं. २०९. In the bank cash book the release is a debit; expenditure, advances and payments over of deductions are credits.

  1. What is appropriation? [1]
  2. What is a budget release? [1]
  3. Write the code for office materials and for furniture. [1]
  4. What is a payment order? [1]
  5. What is an advance (पेस्की)? [1]
  6. What is a गोश्वारा भौचर? [1]
  7. Write the number of the bank cash book format. [1]
  8. Write any two items entered on the debit side of the bank cash book. [1]
  9. What is a statement of expenditure? [1]
  10. How is the available balance of a budget head found? [1]
Answers

1. The amount voted by the legislature for a particular budget head for the financial year.

2. The amount of the appropriation actually made available to the office by the Treasury and Comptroller Office, usually month by month or quarter by quarter.

3. Office materials 22311; furniture and fixtures 31121.

4. The document by which a government office authorises the Treasury and Comptroller Office to pay a stated amount to a stated person against a stated budget head.

5. Money paid to an officer or supplier before the bill is produced; it is a recoverable debt of that person to the government, not an expenditure.

6. The transfer journal voucher used where no money leaves the office — clearing an advance, transferring between heads or adjusting a deposit.

7. म.ले.प.फा.नं. २०९ (A.G.F. No. 209).

8. Any two of: budget release received; revenue deposited; retention and deductions received; refund of an unspent advance; amount transferred in.

9. The monthly return to the Treasury and Comptroller Office showing head by head the annual appropriation, the expenditure to date, the expenditure of the month, the uncleared advances and the available balance.

10. Available balance = annual appropriation − total expenditure to date − uncleared advances.

2.11 Store Accounting

Facts. जिन्सी = goods, consumable and durable. Store ledger = the main book, continuous balance form; bin card = the same record at the shelf; जिन्सी दाखिला फाराम = goods received; जिन्सी निकासा फाराम = goods issued. Verification is annual, by a committee of at least two officers, one unconnected with the store.

  1. What is store accounting? [1]
  2. Write any two importance of store accounting. [1]
  3. Write any two examples of durable store goods. [1]
  4. What is a bin card? [1]
  5. What is a store ledger? [1]
  6. What is the जिन्सी दाखिला फाराम used for? [1]
  7. What is a stock statement? [1]
  8. Who conducts the physical verification of a government store? [1]
  9. May an article be issued from a store without a requisition? [1]
  10. With which record must the bin card always agree? [1]
Answers

1. Store accounting is the branch of government accounting that records the receipt, storage, issue and balance of goods held by a government office, in quantity and in value.

2. Any two of: to record every receipt and issue; to show the stock balance at any time; to prevent loss, misuse and theft; to provide audit evidence; to help budgeting.

3. Any two of: furniture, computers, vehicles, machines, musical instruments.

4. A small card kept on the shelf or bin with the article, showing receipts, issues and the balance in hand.

5. The main store book, with one account or page for each article, showing the date, particulars, receipts, issues and balance.

6. For recording goods received into the store — date, description, specification, quantity, value and supplier.

7. The monthly or periodic statement of goods in hand, by head, sent to the higher office and used for reporting and budgeting.

8. A store inspection committee of at least two officers, one of whom is not connected with the store.

9. No. A written requisition and a signed जिन्सी निकासा फाराम are required.

10. With the store ledger (जिन्सी खाता).

2.12 Fund Accounting and Retention Account

Facts. A fund is a separate pool for a specified purpose. Consolidated fund, contingency fund, divisible fund, retention and deposit fund. Retention is a liability, never revenue. Withheld: expenditure A/c Dr. (full bill); To retention A/c; To bank A/c (net). Released: retention A/c Dr.; To bank A/c. Forfeited: retention A/c Dr.; To repair expenditure A/c and To miscellaneous revenue A/c.

  1. What is a fund? [1]
  2. What is fund accounting? [1]
  3. What is the consolidated fund? [1]
  4. What is the contingency fund used for? [1]
  5. What is the divisible fund? [1]
  6. Which body recommends the shares of the divisible fund? [1]
  7. What is retention? [1]
  8. Write any two kinds of retention. [1]
  9. Show the retention journal voucher at the time the retention money is received (deducted). [1]
  10. Is retention revenue? Give one reason. [1]
Answers

1. A fund is a separate pool of money set aside for a specified purpose and accounted for separately from other money.

2. Fund accounting is the system of keeping a separate account, bank account and statement for each fund, so that its receipts and payments are recorded and reported on their own.

3. The government's main fund, into which all government revenue must be paid and from which nothing may be spent except under an appropriation made by law.

4. To meet unforeseen expenditure, usually while the legislature is not in session; the amount is later regularised by an appropriation.

5. The pool of federal revenue — principally VAT, income tax and royalties — shared with the provinces and the local levels.

6. The National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission.

7. Money withheld from a payment due to a contractor, supplier or employee and held until a stated condition is satisfied.

8. Any two of: goods retention, works (construction) retention, personal retention.

9. Construction (or supplies) expenditure A/c Dr. (full bill); To Contractors' retention A/c (the amount withheld); To Bank / DTCO A/c (the net paid).

10. No. It is a liability of the office to the party from whom it was withheld; it must be returned, or forfeited to revenue only if the condition is not met.

2.13 Internal Control and Auditing

Facts. Internal control = segregation of duties, authorisation, documentation, physical control, reconciliation, supervision, rotation, internal audit. Internal audit is by an employee, continuous, reporting to the management; final audit is by an independent outsider after the year end. The Office of the Auditor General is the apex audit body; its report goes to the President, then to Parliament's Public Accounts Committee.

  1. What is internal control? [1]
  2. Write any two objectives of internal control. [1]
  3. Write any two elements of internal control. [1]
  4. What is an audit? [1]
  5. What is an internal audit? [1]
  6. What is a final audit? [1]
  7. Write any two types of audit on the basis of object. [1]
  8. Which is the apex auditing body of Nepal? [1]
  9. Name the parliamentary committee that examines the audit report. [1]
  10. Who appoints the Auditor General of Nepal? [1]
Answers

1. Internal control is the whole system of policies, procedures, records and checks adopted by an organisation to keep its work accurate, efficient, lawful and honest and to safeguard its assets.

2. Any two of: to safeguard assets; to keep the records accurate and complete; to secure efficiency; to ensure compliance with the law; to prevent and detect fraud and error; to make an audit possible.

3. Any two of: segregation of duties; authorisation; documentation; physical control; reconciliation; supervision; rotation and compulsory leave; internal audit; budget comparison.

4. An audit is an independent examination of the books, records and supporting documents of an organisation so that the auditor may express an opinion on whether the financial statements show a true and fair view.

5. An audit carried out by the organisation's own employees, continuously, to test whether the internal control system is working and whether the records are accurate and the rules followed.

6. The audit carried out after the year end on the completed books and final accounts by an independent external auditor, ending in a report with an opinion.

7. Any two of: financial (regularity) audit, performance audit, management audit, propriety audit.

8. The Office of the Auditor General (महालेखापरीक्षकको कार्यालय).

9. The Public Accounts Committee (सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति).

10. The President, on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council.

2.14 Agencies Involved in Government Accounting

Facts. Ministry of Finance — budget and the consolidated fund. National Planning Commission — plan and ceilings. FCGO — release, central accounts, consolidation, systems. DTCO/PTCO — payments and operating level accounts. Office of the Auditor General — audit. Public Accounts Committee — examination. Nepal Rastra Bank — banker to the government.

  1. Which office prepares the annual budget of the Government of Nepal? [1]
  2. Write any two functions of the Ministry of Finance. [1]
  3. What is the full form of FCGO and what does it do? [1]
  4. What is a DTCO and what does it do? [1]
  5. Which office releases the budget to a spending office? [1]
  6. Who is the banker to the Government of Nepal? [1]
  7. What is the function of the National Planning Commission? [1]
  8. Name the two names of government offices that use central level accounting. [1]
  9. What is the single account fund? [1]
  10. Name the parliamentary committee that examines the audit report. [1]
Answers

1. The Ministry of Finance.

2. Any two of: preparing the budget; framing revenue and fiscal policy; managing the consolidated fund; arranging loans and grants; controlling public expenditure; fixing the terms of government borrowing.

3. Financial Comptroller General Office (महालेखा नियन्त्रक कार्यालय); it releases the budget, keeps the central accounts, supervises the Treasury and Comptroller Offices, consolidates the accounts, maintains the chart of accounts and the formats, and operates the computerised systems.

4. The District Treasury and Comptroller Office; it receives the budget release and makes the payments of the government offices in the district on their payment orders, and keeps the operating level accounts.

5. The Financial Comptroller General Office, through the Treasury and Comptroller Office.

6. Nepal Rastra Bank.

7. The National Planning Commission prepares the country's periodic development plan, sets the priorities and sectoral ceilings for the budget, appraises large projects and recommends the resource envelope.

8. The Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Auditor General (also acceptable: a ministry or department at the centre, and the FCGO).

9. The arrangement under which a government office keeps one designated bank account for all its receipts and payments, recorded in the bank cash book, under the Treasury Single Account.

10. The Public Accounts Committee (सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति).

2.15 Use of Information Technology in Office and Accounting

Facts. Information technology = hardware, software, network, data, people and procedures. Office packages: Word (text), Excel (calculation), PowerPoint (slides), Access (database), Tally and Swastik (accounts). Government systems: BMIS, LMBIS, FMIS, TSA, CGAS, SUTRA, besides PAMS, PMIS, E-GP, ITS and RAS.

  1. What is a computer? [1]
  2. What is information technology? [1]
  3. Write any two components of an information system. [1]
  4. What is an office package? Write any two names. [1]
  5. Write one use of a spreadsheet in an office. [1]
  6. What is the internet? [1]
  7. Write any two advantages of information technology. [1]
  8. Write any two disadvantages of information technology. [1]
  9. Name any two accounting software used in Nepal. [1]
  10. Write the full form of LMBIS or SUTRA. [1]
Answers

1. A computer is an electronic device that accepts data, processes it according to stored instructions, stores the result and gives it out in a usable form.

2. Information technology is the whole set of devices, software, networks and methods by which information is collected, stored, processed and communicated.

3. Any two of: hardware, software, network, data, people, procedures.

4. An office package is a set of application software that does the ordinary work of an office; examples are Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access.

5. Preparing a salary sheet, budget, stock register or bank reconciliation with formulae and totals.

6. The internet is a worldwide network of computers connected so that they can exchange information using common rules.

7. Any two of: speed; accuracy; storage and retrieval; automatic posting; instant reporting; communication; less paper; better control.

8. Any two of: cost; dependence; data loss; fraud and hacking; training; unemployment; health problems; garbage in garbage out; obsolescence.

9. Any two of: Tally, Swastik, Easy Account, Quick Book.

10. LMBIS — Line Ministry Budget Information System; SUTRA — Sub-National Treasury Regulatory Application.
